article_title: The effect of multiple internal representations on context rich instruction
citation: N. Lasry & M.W. Aulls. (2006). The Effect of Multiple Internal Representations on Context Rich Instruction.
title: N-coding: encoding information mentally along multiple dimensions beyond verbal and visual
description: N-coding is a theoretical model of multiple internal mental representations developed from cognitive and imaging studies showing modality-independent information processing. The authors coin the term to extend dual-coding theory: "n-coding... emphasize that 'n' is no longer two (as in dual coding) but the number of encoding dimensions identifiable". Representations can be "verbal, logico-mathematical, visual, kinesthetic, social, etc." The construct was then used to design classroom treatment conditions.
requirements: Instructional environments and problem structures must require activation of multiple n-coding dimensions (e.g. verbal, visual, kinesthetic, social) during task solution
constraints: The authors caution against inferring one-to-one relationships between imaging findings and instructional practice, noting critiques of 'Brain-based' learning
target_learners: algebra-based physics students at a Canadian 2-yr community college
examples: The study applied n-coding by varying the level of representation opportunities in CGPS laboratory sections
key_sources: N. Lasry & M.W. Aulls. (2006). The Effect of Multiple Internal Representations on Context Rich Instruction. https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0605148

article_title: The effect of multiple internal representations on context rich instruction
citation: N. Lasry & M.W. Aulls. (2006). The Effect of Multiple Internal Representations on Context Rich Instruction.
title: Require n-coding (multi-modal processing) in the task solution rather than simulating elaborate life-like environments
description: The article recommends designing ill-structured context-rich problems so students must process information along multiple dimensions (verbal, visual, kinesthetic, social) during problem solution. Its negative result showed that "the processing of information (n-coding tasks) is more important than simulating a life-like environment", so implementations need not include elaborate emulated settings or physical props presented with the problem.
requirements: Students must be able to enquire about or measure needed information during problem solving (as in the medium n-coding condition), collaboratively, in groups of three or four
constraints: The authors caution that guided inquiry presupposes cultural acceptability of active engagement; where formal didactic instruction is culturally expected, such approaches may not succeed
target_learners: introductory algebra-based physics students at community college
examples: The study found that the medium n-coding section, which required enquiry about props without elaborate setups, achieved outcomes not significantly different from the high n-coding section
key_sources: N. Lasry & M.W. Aulls. (2006). The Effect of Multiple Internal Representations on Context Rich Instruction. https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0605148

article_title: Exploring the magnetic field of Helmholtz and Maxwell coils: a computer-based approach exploiting the superposition principle
citation: Jorge Enrique García-Farieta, Alejandro Hurtado-Márquez. (2024). Exploring the magnetic field of Helmholtz and Maxwell coils: a computer-based approach exploiting the superposition principle. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09856
title: The n-wire approach: approximating a circular loop as a regular n-sided polygon of finite wires to compute the magnetic field everywhere
description: The article introduces a hybrid methodology that combines the superposition principle with the analytical field of a finite current-carrying wire. A loop is approximated as a regular n-sides polygon, so the field is 'reduced to the superposition of the field produced by n finite wires carrying the same electric current', which is 'a much simpler problem to solve in the three-dimensional space'. The authors iterate this simple geometry numerically to obtain complex coil systems while 'keeping the physical properties intact', avoiding elliptic integrals and advanced calculus.
requirements: The current-carrying system must be expressible geometrically as a superposition of n finite wires
constraints: The polygonal approximation approaches the true circular-loop field only in the limit n → ∞, as shown for the field at the loop center
target_learners: undergraduate physics and engineering students in introductory electromagnetism courses
target_learning_goals: evaluate the magnetic field of current-carrying systems at any point in space using the Biot-Savart law and the superposition principle
examples: The approach was applied to Helmholtz coils (two coils) and Maxwell coils (three coils) approximated by regular polygons of 80 sides inside a meshgrid of 50^3 points
key_sources: Jorge Enrique García-Farieta, Alejandro Hurtado-Márquez. (2024). Exploring the magnetic field of Helmholtz and Maxwell coils: a computer-based approach exploiting the superposition principle. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09856
